'''John Robertson''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name=royal/> (born 1950) is a professor of [[electronics]], in the [[Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge|Department of Engineering]] at the [[University of Cambridge]]. He is a leading specialist in the theory of amorphous carbon and related materials.<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus|id= 55763673600}}</ref><ref name=engcam/><ref name=cam/>

==Education==
Robertson received his Bachelor of Arts and Doctor of Philosophy<ref name=robphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=Electronic States in Amorphous Semi-Conductors|first= John|last=Robertson|year=1975|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.470683|oclc=500550417}}</ref> degrees from the University of Cambridge. His PhD was awarded in 1975 for research on [[energy level|electronic states]] in [[Amorphous solid|amorphous]] [[semiconductor]]s.<ref name=robphd/>

==Research and career==
Following his PhD, Robertson worked at the [[Central Electricity Research Laboratories]] for 18 years,{{citation needed|date=May 2015}} and in 1994 returned to Cambridge. He has published over 600 journal papers with around 33,000 citations.<ref name=scopus/> His main topic of research is theory of carbon materials.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.61.14095| title = Interpretation of Raman spectra of disordered and amorphous carbon| journal = Physical Review B| volume = 61| issue = 20| article-number = 14095| year = 2000| last1 = Ferrari | first1 = A.| last2 = Robertson | first2 = J.| bibcode = 2000PhRvB..6114095F}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/S0927-796X(02)00005-0| title = Diamond-like amorphous carbon| journal = Materials Science and Engineering: R: Reports| volume = 37| issue = 4–6| pages = 129–281| year = 2002| last1 = Robertson | first1 = J. | s2cid = 135487365| author-link1 = John Robertson (physicist)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1116/1.591472| title = Band offsets of wide-band-gap oxides and implications for future electronic devices| journal = Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology B: Microelectronics and Nanometer Structures| volume = 18| issue = 3| pages = 1785–1791| year = 2000| last1 = Robertson | first1 = J. | bibcode = 2000JVSTB..18.1785R}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1080/00018738600101911| title = Amorphous carbon| journal = [[Advances in Physics]]| volume = 35| issue = 4| pages = 317–374| year = 1986| last1 = Robertson | first1 = J. | author-link1 = John Robertson (physicist)| bibcode = 1986AdPhy..35..317R}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevB.35.2946| pmid = 9941778| title = Electronic and atomic structure of amorphous carbon| journal = Physical Review B| volume = 35| issue = 6| pages = 2946–2957| year = 1987| last1 = Robertson | first1 = J.| last2 = O'Reilly | first2 = E.| bibcode = 1987PhRvB..35.2946R}}</ref> Other research interests include: carbon nanotubes, graphene, [[chemical vapor deposition|chemical vapour deposition]], electronic applications (experimental and calculation); modelling of CVD mechanisms; carbon interconnects, carbon conductors, carbon for [[supercapacitor]]s; [[high-κ dielectric]]s for complementary [[MOSFET|metal oxide semiconductor transistor]]s; high-κ oxides on high mobility substrates such as [[Indium gallium arsenide|InGaAs]], [[Germanium|Ge]] (modelling); transparent conducting oxides, amorphous oxide semiconductors (AOS) such as [[indium gallium zinc oxide]], their thin film transistors, instability mechanisms (calculations); density functional calculations of semiconductors, oxides, carbon materials, and hybrid density functional calculations for correct [[band gap]]s; functional oxides, [[Titanium dioxide|TiO<sub>2</sub>]].<ref name=cam>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150529094626/http://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/news/royal-society-fellows-professors-john-robertson-and-zoubin-ghahramani|archive-date=2015-05-29|url=http://www.eng.cam.ac.uk/news/royal-society-fellows-professors-john-robertson-and-zoubin-ghahramani|title=Congratulations to Professors John Robertson and Zoubin Ghahramani on their elections as Fellows of the Royal Society|date=13 May 2015 |publisher=University of Cambridge}}</ref><ref name=engcam>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141009193811/http://www-g.eng.cam.ac.uk/edm/people/index.php|archive-date=2014-10-09|url=http://www-g.eng.cam.ac.uk/edm/people/index.php|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=People in the Electronic Devices and Materials group}}</ref>

His research has been funded by the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC)]].<ref name=gtr>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150529131207/http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/33D4FC2D-8EDC-4700-B3F0-4D5FA3DBD73F|archive-date=2015-05-29|url=http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/33D4FC2D-8EDC-4700-B3F0-4D5FA3DBD73F|title=UK Government Research Grants awarded to John Robertson|publisher=[[Research Councils UK]]}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Robertson is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)]] and the [[Materials Research Society]], and an emeritus editor of the journal ''Diamond and Related Materials''.<ref>[http://www.journals.elsevier.com/diamond-and-related-materials/editorial-board/ Diamond and Related Materials Editorial Board]. journals.elsevier.com</ref> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2015|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2015]],<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117101431/https://royalsociety.org/people/john-robertson-12192/|archive-date=2015-11-17|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/john-robertson-12192/|title=Professor John Robertson FRS|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}}</ref> his certificate of election reads: "In recognition of his sustained contribution to the production and development of electronic devices".<ref name=royal>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2015/andrew-cooper/ |title = Professor John Robertson FRS |publisher=The Royal Society |archive-date=2015-05-02 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150502203922/https://royalsociety.org/people/fellowship/2015/john-robertson/ |location=London}}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor John Robertson FREng FRS |url=https://raeng.org.uk/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2020/professor-john-robertson-freng-frs |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=Royal Academy of Engineering |language=en}}</ref>
